Objective: Verify post-reset initialization state after active-low synchronous reset (RST_i=0) and ensure the 7-stage valid pipeline v_pipe_r is completely cleared without emitting spurious out_valid_o pulses.
Stimulus: Hold RST_i=0 for 10 clock cycles while driving random data onto acc_i/bias_i/mult_i/shift_i/zp_i with in_valid_i=1; then release RST_i=1 and hold in_valid_i=0 for 15 cycles.
Checks: Monitor out_valid_o throughout reset and for 15 cycles after reset release; check that no X/Z values appear on out_valid_o.
Expected_result: out_valid_o remains strictly 0 throughout reset and across all 15 idle cycles after reset release.
Notes: Confirms v_pipe_r[6:0] is cleared to 0 when !RST_i.
Bug_Injection_Target: Removing the if (!RST_i) reset branch of v_pipe_r at line 107 -> TB catches out_valid_o=1 or X after reset.
Pass_Criteria: out_valid_o == 0 in every cycle; 0 X/Z errors.

Objective: Verify the exact pipeline latency of L=7 clock cycles from a single in_valid_i=1 pulse to the resulting out_valid_o=1 pulse.
Stimulus: Assert a single 1-cycle pulse in_valid_i=1 at cycle T0 with a known 16-channel input vector, then hold in_valid_i=0 for 20 cycles. Repeat 10 times with random idle gaps of 1..10 cycles.
Checks: Count clock cycles from the rising CLK_i edge sampling in_valid_i=1 to the rising CLK_i edge where out_valid_o=1; check out_valid_o pulse width.
Expected_result: out_valid_o asserts to 1 for exactly 1 cycle at T0 + 7 cycles; out_data_o matches the golden result 100% on that exact cycle.
Notes: Matches the C_DRAIN FSM timing in l2_tiling_agu.v.
Bug_Injection_Target: Changing v_pipe_r[L-2] to v_pipe_r[L-3] at lines 98/112 (latency 6 instead of 7) -> TB reports cycle-latency mismatch.
Pass_Criteria: Measured latency = 7 cycles for every pulse; pulse width = 1 cycle.

Objective: Verify sustained back-to-back streaming capability of 1 row (16 channels) per clock cycle (throughput = 1 row/cycle) with no data collision across pipeline stages S1..S7.
Stimulus: Hold in_valid_i=1 continuously for 256 cycles, driving a distinct set of 16-channel acc_i, bias_i, mult_i, shift_i, and zp_i vectors every cycle.
Checks: From cycle T0+7 to T0+262, compare each 128-bit out_data_o row against the golden FIFO queue; verify out_valid_o stays at 1 continuously for 256 cycles.
Expected_result: All 256 consecutive output rows exit without missing a single beat and match golden byte-for-byte across all 16 channels.
Notes: Proves the 7 pipeline register stages t1..y6 advance independently without overwriting one another.
Golden_Reference_Rule: Output row k at cycle (T0+7+k) == golden(input row k).
Bug_Injection_Target: Bypassing intermediate pipeline stage p3_r (connecting p2_r directly to r4_r) -> TB reports data mismatch during back-to-back streaming.
Pass_Criteria: 256/256 rows match bit-exact; out_valid_o=1 continuously for 256 cycles.

Objective: Verify backward compatibility with legacy per-tensor rescaling when configured with mult=1, bias=0, zp=zero_point, and shift=scale_shift.
Stimulus: Set bias_i=0 and mult_i=1 across all 16 channels, sweep shift_i from 0 to 24 and zp_i in {-128, -1, 0, 1, 127}, and drive 1,000 random acc_i vectors.
Checks: Compare out_data_o against the per-tensor rounding right-shift formula: clamp(((acc + (shift?1<<(shift-1):0)) >>> shift) + zp, -128, 127).
Expected_result: Results match the per-tensor formula 100% across all 1,000 vectors x 16 channels.
Notes: Follows the design note at lines 16-17 of the RTL.
Bug_Injection_Target: Misconfiguring default mult_i or inverting zp_i sign -> TB reports mismatch.

Objective: Verify the shift=0 boundary case: no rounding offset may be added (rnd_v=0) and no negative left-shift (1 <<< -1) may occur.
Stimulus: Set shift_i=0 for all 16 channels; drive (acc, bias, mult, zp) tuples such that product p spans [-200, +200] including odd, even, negative, and positive values.
Checks: Verify rnd_v=0 when s3_r==0 (line 86) and q5_r == p3_r (line 91); compare out_data_o against clamp((acc+bias)*mult + zp, -128, 127).
Expected_result: When shift=0, division by 2^0 preserves the exact product p3_r without adding 1 or 0.5.
Notes: Critical corner case because without the ternary operator at line 86, (s3_r - 1) would underflow to 6'd63.
Bug_Injection_Target: Removing the (s3_r[i] == 6'd0) ? 66'sd0 guard at line 86 -> TB immediately reports FAIL on test RQ_005.
Pass_Criteria: 100% of channels match golden when shift=0.

Objective: Verify shift=1 (divide by 2, round-half-up tie-breaking with rnd_v = 1) at exact odd integer boundaries (...-3, -2, -1, 0, +1, +2, +3...).
Stimulus: Set shift_i=1, mult_i=1, bias_i=0, zp_i=0; sweep acc_i across all integers from -256 to +256 (even and odd, negative and positive).
Expected_result: All half-way cases (remainder 0.5) round up toward +infinity (+0.5 -> +1, -0.5 -> 0, -1.5 -> -1) in exact accordance with round-half-up.
Notes: Validates the exact rounding direction (round-half-up toward +infinity) shared by the RTL and C++ runtime.
Bug_Injection_Target: Changing + rnd_v at line 87 to round-half-to-even or truncation -> TB reports FAIL on odd inputs.

Objective: Verify the upper shift boundary (shift=62) and confirm the RTL extracts only the lower 6 bits shift_i[5:0], ignoring upper bits shift_i[7:6].
Stimulus: Run 2 passes with the same large 64-bit product: pass 1 sets shift_i = 8'd62 (0x3E); pass 2 sets shift_i = 8'hFE (upper 2 bits = 2'b11, lower 6 bits = 62). Also sweep shift = 31, 32, 61, 62.
Checks: Verify pass 1 and pass 2 produce identical outputs; at shift=62, rnd_v = 1<<61 is added accurately in the 66-bit signed register r4_r without sign overflow.
Expected_result: Results at shift=62 match 128-bit reference math; garbage bits in shift_i[7:6] are completely masked out by shift_i[i*8 +: 6].
Notes: At shift=62, 66'sd1 <<< 61 sets bit 61 of rnd_v, requiring the 66-bit signed register r4_r.
Bug_Injection_Target: Narrowing r4_r from 66 bits to 64 bits or reading 7 bits of shift_i -> TB reports FAIL at shift=62.
Pass_Criteria: 100% match between shift=0x3E and 0xFE and against 128-bit golden.

Objective: Verify Stage S1: 33-bit signed addition t1_r = acc + bias does not overflow (wrap around) when both acc and bias are at INT32_MAX or INT32_MIN boundaries.
Checks: Verify t1_r preserves +4,294,967,294 (for MAX+MAX) and -4,294,967,296 (for MIN+MIN) by checking the output after right-shifting by 32 bits.
Expected_result: MAX+MAX after shift=32 yields +1; MIN+MIN after shift=32 yields -1; MAX+MIN yields 0. Zero 32-bit wrap-around overflow occurs.
Notes: If added in 32-bit precision before sign-extension, MAX+MAX would wrap around to -2 (inverting the sign completely).
Bug_Injection_Target: Omitting sign-extension bit acc_i[i*32+31] at line 72 (pure 32-bit add) -> TB catches the sign inversion immediately.

Objective: Verify Stage S2/S3: 33-bit x 32-bit -> 65-bit signed multiplication p2_r = t1_r * m1_r at maximum positive and negative extremes.
Stimulus: Combine t1_r at boundaries {-2^32, +2^32-2, -1, 0, +1} with mult_i at boundaries {-2^31 (0x80000000), +2^31-1 (0x7FFFFFFF), -1, 0, +1} and shift in 55..62.
Checks: Compare the right-shifted outputs against the 128-bit signed arithmetic reference model in SystemVerilog.
Expected_result: The 65-bit product preserves the exact sign at bit 64 across all neg*neg, neg*pos, pos*neg, and pos*pos combinations.
Notes: The largest product is (-2^32) * (-2^31) = +2^63, which requires a full 65-bit signed representation to hold positive +2^63.
Bug_Injection_Target: Reducing p2_r/p3_r width from [64:0] to [63:0] -> (-2^32)*(-2^31) overflows to -2^63 -> TB reports FAIL.

Objective: Verify rounding addition r4_r and arithmetic right-shift >>> accuracy across both negative and positive domains right around the 0.5 LSB threshold.
Stimulus: For each shift in {2, 7, 15, 24, 31, 48}, construct products p = k*(2^shift) + delta with delta in {2^(shift-1)-1, 2^(shift-1), 2^(shift-1)+1} for both negative k (-100..-1) and positive k (0..100).
Checks: Verify that at delta = 2^(shift-1)-1 the result rounds down to k, while at delta = 2^(shift-1) and 2^(shift-1)+1 the result rounds up to k+1.
Expected_result: Zero 1-LSB (off-by-one) errors on either side of the 2^(shift-1) midpoint.
coverage_target: cg_round: below_half_lsb, exact_half_lsb, above_half_lsb x {pos, neg} (100%)
Notes: This is the most common hardware requantizer bug (using logical >> instead of arithmetic >>> or an off-by-one shift in rnd_v).
Bug_Injection_Target: Replacing >>> at line 91 with >> or changing (s3_r[i] - 6'd1) to s3_r[i] -> TB reports FAIL immediately.
Pass_Criteria: 0 1-LSB errors across the entire sweep grid.

Objective: Verify upper saturation clamping (Upper Clamp = +127 / 8'h7F) in Stage S6/S7 across near-boundary values and maximum 66-bit positive overflow values.
Stimulus: Construct inputs such that y6_r = q5_r + z5_r evaluates to: 125, 126, 127, 128, 129, 255, 32767, and maximum +2^64 (when shift=0, acc=MAX, mult=MAX, zp=MAX).
Checks: Verify that y6_r = 126 -> 126; y6_r = 127 -> 127 (0x7F); and all y6_r >= 128 clamp firmly to 8'h7F (127) without wrapping around to negative numbers.
Expected_result: out_data_o equals 8'h7E (126) when y=126, and 8'h7F (127) for all y >= 127.
Notes: Ensures the 67-bit register y6_r never suffers sign overflow when adding q5_r (66-bit) and z5_r (32-bit).
Bug_Injection_Target: Changing line 99 from (y_v > 67'sd127) to (y_v >= 67'sd127) or omitting sign-extension of q5_r at line 94 -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: All boundary points 126, 127, 128, and positive extremes match 100%.

Objective: Verify lower saturation clamping (Lower Clamp = -128 / 8'h80) in Stage S6/S7 across near-boundary values and minimum 66-bit negative underflow values.
Stimulus: Construct inputs such that y6_r = q5_r + z5_r evaluates to: -126, -127, -128, -129, -130, -256, -32768, and minimum -2^64 (when shift=0, acc=MIN, mult=MAX, zp=MIN).
Expected_result: out_data_o equals 8'h81 when y=-127, and 8'h80 (-128) for all y <= -128 without wrapping to positive values.
Notes: Symmetric check to RQ_011 at the negative INT8 boundary.
Bug_Injection_Target: Changing line 100 from (y_v < -67'sd128) to (y_v < -67'sd127) -> TB reports FAIL at y=-128.
Pass_Criteria: All boundary points -127, -128, -129, and negative extremes match 100%.

Objective: Verify 32-bit signed zero-point (zp_i) addition in Stage S6 with 35-bit sign extension ({35{z5_r[31]}}, z5_r).
Stimulus: Hold q5_r within [-200, +200] and sweep zp_i across {-128, -1, 0, +1, +127, +1000, -1000, INT32_MAX, INT32_MIN}.
Checks: Verify sign-extension of z5_r to 67 bits at line 95 works properly for both negative and positive zp, and Stage S7 saturation clamping handles large zp values accurately.
Expected_result: Results match clamp(q + zp, -128, 127) 100% across all negative and positive zp cases.
Notes: In Qwen2-Audio P1.5, zp is typically 0 for symmetric quantization or within [-128, 127] for asymmetric quantization.
Bug_Injection_Target: Replacing {35{z5_r[31]}} at line 95 with 35'd0 (zero-extending instead of sign-extending) -> negative zp values add as large positive numbers -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: 0 errors across all zp test values.

Objective: Verify complete independence across all 16 lanes (lanes 0..15) when each lane carries opposing (bias, mult, shift, zp) parameters and acc data.
Stimulus: In each cycle, configure even lanes for extreme positive/negative saturation or shift=0 while configuring odd lanes for normal scaling with shift=20..30; rotate lane assignments across 16 cycles (walking-lane test).
Checks: Verify each lane i depends solely on its own bit slice [i*32 +: 32] (or [i*8 +: 8]) and is completely unaffected by overflow or saturation in adjacent lanes i-1 or i+1.
Expected_result: All 16/16 lanes produce independent outputs matching individual per-lane golden calculations 100%.
Notes: Confirms bit-slice indexing [i*32 +: 32] and [i*8 +: 8] inside the for (i=0; i<N; i++) loop is completely accurate.
Golden_Reference_Rule: out_lane[i] == golden_lane(acc[i], bias[i], mult[i], shift[i], zp[i]) for all i in 0..15.
Bug_Injection_Target: Mistyping shift_i[i*8 +: 6] as shift_i[0 +: 6] (sharing lane 0 shift across all lanes) -> TB reports FAIL on lanes 1..15.

Objective: Verify out_data_o value-holding behavior during pipeline bubbles (intermittent in_valid_i=0) and verify packet cancellation when asserting RST_i=0 while the pipeline is populated.
Stimulus: Part A: Drive a random in_valid_i sequence (30% valid probability) while driving garbage on data ports whenever in_valid_i=0. Part B: Feed 5 consecutive valid rows (in_valid_i=1), assert RST_i=0 for 2 cycles on cycle 4, then release reset and feed a new batch.
Checks: Part A: Verify in_valid_i=0 cycles never produce out_valid_o=1 and out_data_o holds its previous valid value (via if (v_pipe_r[L-2]) at line 98). Part B: All 5 pre-reset rows are cleanly aborted and the post-reset batch computes accurately.
Expected_result: Zero spurious out_valid_o pulses; garbage data during in_valid_i=0 cycles never corrupts outputs; pipeline recovers 100% cleanly after mid-flight reset.
Notes: Directly tests line 98: if (v_pipe_r[L-2]) updates out_data_o only when valid data reaches the final stage.
Golden_Reference_Rule: out_valid_o asserts only for beats that exited before RST_i=0 or new beats entering after RST_i=1.
Bug_Injection_Target: Removing if (v_pipe_r[L-2]) at line 98 -> out_data_o is overwritten by garbage during idle cycles -> hold-value check catches it.
Pass_Criteria: 0 spurious valid pulses; 100% of post-reset packets are accurate.

Objective: Run an exhaustive constrained-random regression (100,000 rows = 1.6 million requantization operations) combining the real parameter distribution of Qwen2-Audio INT8 P1.5 with full-range 32-bit random stimuli.
Stimulus: Run 100,000 cycles with a configurable seed (+SEED=): 50% drawn from the real Qwen2-Audio distribution (acc in [-2^24, +2^24], mult in [2^29, 2^31-1], shift in [28..42], zp=0) and 50% full-range 32-bit random with a 20% saturation rate.
Checks: Automatically compare every byte across all 1,600,000 channel outputs against the 128-bit golden reference function; verify all functional coverage bins hit 100%.
Expected_result: All 100,000 rows (1,600,000 channel operations) match bit-exact 100% (0 mismatches); functional coverage reaches 100%.
Notes: Final sign-off test certifying absolute reliability of the Requant unit prior to integration into l2_tiling_agu.
Golden_Reference_Rule: 100% bit-exact match with C++ rq1() in llm_runtime.cpp and the 128-bit SystemVerilog golden function.
Bug_Injection_Target: Any arithmetic, rounding, or saturation bug across the 7 pipeline stages is exposed by these 1.6 million samples.
